errors.description: The spanning tree is not shown to index a directed system, so Lemma 3.6 cannot be applied to obtain the asserted direct limit. An orientation of a tree can have vertices in different branches with no common successor in that tree; directedness of the full f-simple poset does not make the selected tree directed.
errors.evidence: The proof says the spanning tree yields a “directed acyclic subquiver T'” and then “This gives a directed system of f-simples ... therefore we can use Lemma 3.6.” A directed acyclic quiver need not be a directed indexing set: the two vertices in separate outward branches may have no common upper bound in T'. Lemma 3.6 assumes a direct system, which requires a directed index category. Thus the construction does not establish an F containing every f-simple, a key step in the proposition.
